Average speeds over equal time intervals

officialSolution.label: 2018 AMC 10B

question: Sam drove \(96\) miles in \(90\) minutes. His average speed during the first \(30\) minutes was \(60\) mph (miles per hour), and his average speed during the second \(30\) minutes was \(65\) mph. What was his average speed, in mph, during the last \(30\) minutes?
solution:
Each \(30\)-minute interval is \(\tfrac12\) hour, so use distance equals speed times time to find the first two distances:
\[
60\cdot\frac12=30\text{ miles},\qquad
65\cdot\frac12=32.5\text{ miles}.
\]
The distance left for the last half hour was
\[
96-30-32.5=33.5\text{ miles}.
\]
Dividing this distance by its travel time gives the last interval's average speed:
\[
\frac{33.5}{1/2}=67\text{ mph}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{67}\), choice D.
